correctness.rationale: The distinct-root hypothesis guarantees a unique relation with nonzero coefficients among any matched dependent quadratics, and the explicit Q_i solve the Weierstrass differences. Six simple zeros yield six I_2 fibers and a rational elliptic surface. A trace-zero Möbius matrix proves equivalence to three paired roots, and the genus-two involution lifts/descends without fixed branch points. The symmetric fifteen-factor product descends to a degree-15 polynomial; incidence irreducibility, distinct factors and a nonvanishing collision show irreducible reduced closure. Generic matching uniqueness gives a birational inverse. The exact code was replayed, with no finite experiment used as a universal proof.
